definitions.explanation: A reflective surface for seeing one's image.

examples.japanese: {鏡|かがみ}に{自分|じぶん}の{顔|かお}が{映|うつ}っている。
examples.english: My face is reflected in the mirror.

examples.japanese: {鏡|かがみ}が{割|わ}れてしまった。
{朝|あさ}、{鏡|かがみ}の{前|まえ}で{髪|かみ}を{整|ととの}えてから{出|で}かける。
examples.english: In the morning, I fix my hair in front of the mirror before going out.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{服|ふく}を{買|か}ったので、{鏡|かがみ}の{前|まえ}で{何度|なんど}も{着|き}てみて、うれしそうにしていた。
examples.english: I bought new clothes and happily tried them on over and over in front of the mirror.

notes:
{鏡|かがみ} means mirror.

CULTURE:
Mirrors are one of the three sacred treasures of Japan ({三種|さんしゅ}の{神器|じんぎ}).

COMPOUNDS:
- {手鏡|てかがみ}: hand mirror
- {姿見|すがたみ}: full-length mirror
- {鏡餅|かがみもち}: New Year's rice cakes

EXPRESSIONS:
- {人|ひと}の{振|ふ}り{見|み}て{我|わ}が{振|ふ}り{直|なお}せ}: learn from others' mistakes
